level_description: Advanced Language Features (Targets DSL constructs that are unit-tested at the compiler level but were never exercised by any of the other 38 benchmark cases against a real model: the standalone `invariant { }` block combined with the implication operator (->), membership against a computed/non-literal set (IN this.<field>), exclusion (NIN), and the Array<T>/Map<K,V> collection types. Building this suite surfaced three genuine, previously-unknown compiler/runtime bugs -- fixed as part of this work, not worked around: (1) the binder rejected `Integer` fields using `IN` against a literal list, because every numeric literal binds to Number regardless of how it was written, so an exact BuiltinType match could never succeed; (2) a standalone invariant block's implication (e.g. the CloudProvision worked example from the Methodology chapter) could be scheduled and checked before the field it depends on was ever assigned, silently never enforcing the rule -- the CloudProvision spec, exactly as written, did not compile before this fix; (3) `Modulo` parsed but had no evaluator case, throwing at runtime. ADV_cloud_provision is the Methodology chapter's own worked example, run against a real model for the first time. ADV_freeform_array_stress and ADV_freeform_map_stress deliberately probe Array<T>/Map<K,V> under free (non-deterministic) LLM generation, where the mask has no dedicated structural logic at all -- an empty-buffer test showed 93,260 of ~150,000 vocab tokens pass unrestricted for an Array<Integer> field, meaning the 'always valid JSON' guarantee does not hold for these types unless they are fully AOT-solved. Map<K,V> additionally has no literal expression syntax at all, so it cannot even be pinned to an exact deterministic value -- these two cases are expected to show real, honest weaknesses, not pass cleanly.

ADV_cloud_provision.name: Cloud Provisioning (Methodology worked example)
ADV_cloud_provision.description: The dissertation's own CloudProvision worked example (Methodology chapter), run against a real model for the first time -- previously only hand-traced. Exercises: `invariant { }` blocks, IN against a literal list, and the implication operator (->) gating tier based on a deterministically-computed total_ram. Required a binder fix (Integer vs Number literal typing) and a scheduler fix (invariant-block implication ordering) to compile and behave correctly at all.

prompts.system: You are a cloud infrastructure provisioning service generating a validated resource allocation. Output ONLY raw, valid JSON.
prompts.user: Generate a cloud resource allocation for a compute cluster: pick a base RAM per instance (at least 8 GB) and an instance count, then classify the deployment tier.

ADV_membership_and_exclusion.name: Firewall Port Selection (IN / NIN against a computed set)
ADV_membership_and_exclusion.description: allowed_ports is a deterministic Array<Integer> (exact-value literal, AOT-solved -- never freely typed by the model). chosen_port must be IN that computed array; blocked_port must be NIN it. Neither `IN this.<field>` nor `NIN` against a non-literal set had been exercised by any prior case.

prompts.system: You are a network firewall configuration service. Output ONLY raw, valid JSON.
prompts.user: Generate a firewall rule pair: pick one port to explicitly allow from the standard web ports, and one port in the 1-100 range to explicitly block that is NOT one of the standard web ports.

blocked_port.description: Must NOT be one of allowed_ports

ADV_freeform_array_stress.name: Freely-Sampled Array Stress Test
ADV_freeform_array_stress.description: A deliberate probe, not an expected pass: `tags` has NO constraint at all, forcing the model to freely type an Array<String> value token-by-token with no deterministic escape hatch. The mask has no dedicated structural logic for Complex (Array/Map/Spec) types -- confirmed by a direct test showing 93,260 of ~150,000 vocab tokens pass unrestricted for an empty Array<Integer> buffer. This case documents what actually happens under real generation: possibly a malformed/unparseable value, possibly a lucky well-formed one, but not a guaranteed-valid one.

prompts.system: You are a content tagging service generating a validated set of tags. Output ONLY raw, valid JSON.
prompts.user: Generate a list of 3-5 short tags for a blog post about home coffee brewing.

ADV_freeform_map_stress.name: Freely-Sampled Map Stress Test
ADV_freeform_map_stress.description: A deliberate probe, not an expected pass: `settings` has NO constraint (none is even expressible -- the language has no map-literal expression syntax, so a Map<K,V> field can never be pinned to an exact deterministic value the way an Array<T> field can). Same masking gap as ADV_freeform_array_stress, but for a type with no AOT escape hatch whatsoever.

prompts.system: You are a device configuration service generating validated settings. Output ONLY raw, valid JSON.
prompts.user: Generate a settings map with 2-3 key-value pairs for a thermostat device (e.g. target temperature, mode).
